headline: All majors below 200-day lines with neutral momentum; whales loading Bitcoin onto exchanges while funding stays positive.
paragraphs: The market regime is uniformly bearish. All seven assets in the board sit below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none have achieved a golden cross. Bitcoin trades at 63,653.85, down 0.34% on the day and 49% from its 12-month high of 124,773.51. Ethereum at 1,904.72 is 60.6% below that peak. Solana, the hardest hit on the major list, sits 70.4% below its year high. The entire structure is inverted: price below the long-term trend line across the board, with Bitcoin dominance at 56.7% holding steady and total market cap essentially flat at a 0.19% daily gain. This is a market that has not reclaimed its intermediate trend.

Momentum readings reveal a market at rest rather than accelerating downward. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 47.4, Ethereum at 56.3, and Solana at 42.7: all within neutral territory, neither oversold nor overbought. The tension: MACD is underwater on five of seven assets (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, Cardano) but positive on two (BNB and Doge). This divergence matters. BNB and Doge both show MACD above signal despite price weakness and no golden cross, a classic setup where momentum is staging a small lift beneath a falling trend. For the majority, MACD and price are aligned in weakness, but there is no acceleration. The 24-hour and 7-day moves are small: Bitcoin down 1.59% over the week, Ethereum up 1.81%, Solana down 4.01%. Nothing is plunging; nothing is recovering with conviction.

Derivatives positioning shows long-biased crowding with near-neutral funding. Bitcoin funding is 0.01% per 8-hour period, annualizing to 10.9%, which is positive but not excessive. Ethereum's 0.0045% 8h print (4.9% annual) is calmer still. More telling is the long-short ratio: Bitcoin 1.14 to 1, Ethereum 1.33 to 1, but Solana 2.01 to 1, XRP 3.61 to 1, and Doge 4.99 to 1. The megacap longs are modestly overweight; the smaller assets are heavily skewed to long leverage. Over the last 24 hours, liquidations hit more shorts than longs across all five tracked assets, with Ethereum recording 3.92 million dollars in short liquidations versus 1.24 million in long liquidations. Open interest remains substantial: Bitcoin at 2.08 billion dollars, Ethereum at 1.29 billion. The boat is full, the long side is crowded, and funding is barely paying to hold. This is not a cheap setup, and the liquidation pattern (shorts getting flushed more than longs) suggests the market is testing short stops rather than confirming conviction.

Whale and institutional flows tell a story that contradicts the momentum picture. Over the past 48 hours, 65 million dollars in Bitcoin has moved onto exchanges, all of it to Binance. This is not the pattern of accumulation into cold storage or long-term holders building a position; it is supply arriving at the door. However, the weekly net context complicates the read: the most recent week shows negative 86.7 million dollars net onto exchanges, but the three prior weeks ran positive (385.7 million, 1.075 billion, 67.2 million dollars outflow). The longer 30-day stablecoin float is stable at 306.2 billion dollars, down only 1.03% from 30 days prior. Buying power has not collapsed, but neither is it being drawn. Bitcoin ETF flows remain positive: 101.7 million dollars on 07 August and 865.3 million over the last five sessions, all five days inflow. This is traditional finance steady buying while spot markets tread water and whales backload exchanges. The two systems are not synchronized.

Sentiment stands at 31, labeled Fear, in a 30-day range of 22 to 33. The crowd is scared but not panicked. The Fear & Greed index is near the low of its recent band, yet price has not crashed, and leverage has not blown up. This is a disconnect worth watching: fear that has not yet led to capitulation, positioned longs that have not yet been forced out, and spot buying from institutions that is not translating to spot price recovery. The small-cap movers (BEAT up 36.2%, PUMP up 13.8%) suggest retail chasing low-liquidity names, a behavior typical of early-stage fear rather than despair.

The condition to monitor: a Bitcoin MACD cross above signal while price remains below 200-day SMA would signal momentum lift within the downtrend, a prerequisite for any sustained recovery. Watch the whale 48-hour flow window: if the 65 million dollars moving onto Binance accelerates, supply pressure is building and could extend the weakness. If inflows reverse this week back to outflow (as the three prior weeks showed), the tape reverts to a constructive bias despite sentiment. Track the short liquidations: if longs begin taking damage alongside shorts, crowding is unwinding. Finally, stablecoin float is the margin reserve: any sharp move higher signals dry powder returning to buy, and any move lower signals cash exiting. Today's picture is stalled recovery, not broken downtrend, and not fresh accumulation. The next move will announce itself first in derivatives unwinding or whale direction, not in spot price.
